data.name: Harshavardhan
data.gender_notes: Harshavardhan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Harshavardhan is a combination of two Sanskrit words: Harsh (Lord) and Vardhan (Nourisher). The name signifies the one who nourishes and protects the gods and the devotees. The name Harshavardhan carries the meaning “Lord of the Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Harshavardhan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Harshavardhan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harshavardhan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Harshavardhan has great significance in Hindu mythology and culture. Harsh in the name symbolizes Lord Vishnu and his role as the supreme protector and preserver of the universe. Vardhan signifies the provider and nourisher, which is a reflection of Lord Vishnu's role as the giver of sustenance and life to all beings. The name is commonly associated with Lord Krishna, an incarnation of Vishnu, who is known to have nourished and protected his devotees.
data.spiritual_significance: Harshavardhan is a name that evokes a sense of protection, strength, and faith. It reminds us of the concept of God as the ultimate protector and provider, and encourages us to seek refuge in His divine presence. The name also encourages us to reflect on our own role as providers and nourishers in our own lives, inspiring us to act with kindness, compassion, and generosity towards others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Harshavardhan: Radiant and severe Vishnu. The name signifies the divine balance between love and compassion (Harsha) and absolute authority and power (Vardhan).

vedic_reference.root_origin: Vardhan is a form of Lord Vishnu
vedic_reference.note: Harshavardhan is a revered name in Hinduism, derived from Lord Vishnu's form Vardhan. He is often depicted with a conch shell and a mace in his hands, symbolizing the power to bestow joy and protect his devotees.

historical_references.reference: Harshavardhan was the name of the famous Indian emperor Harshadeva, also known as Harshavardhana. He ruled over a vast empire from 606 to 647 AD, during which time he established a center of culture and learning in Kaushambi, near present-day Allahabad.
historical_references.context: Established a center of culture and learning in Kaushambi

historical_references.reference: Harshavardhan was a great patron of art and learning. He is credited with the authorship of several books, including the Jitendriya Prakasha, a Sanskrit encyclopedia and the Harshacharita, an autobiography that is a major source of information about his reign.
historical_references.context: Great patron of art and learning
